pure-announcement.rationale: This is a peer-style arXiv research study with methodology and findings, not a product launch or release note.

duplicate.rationale: None of the nearest concepts (RAG, Ebbinghaus forgetting curve, LLM-maintained wiki, etc.) cover empirical evidence of reduced neural engagement from LLM-assisted writing.

unfalsifiable.rationale: Claims trace to a primary arXiv paper (2506.08872) with a described EEG protocol, participant counts, and session design a reader can check.

durability.rationale: The mechanism-level finding — cognitive engagement and memory scale down as writing is offloaded to an LLM, and unaided-first ordering preserves them — is an empirical result that will not expire with model versions.

actionability.rationale: The abstract mainly documents a phenomenon and raises concerns; the practice implication (do unaided work before invoking the LLM) is implied by the Brain-to-LLM result but never stated as a usable pattern.

atomicity.rationale: One core idea — LLM assistance accumulates cognitive debt measurable in connectivity, recall, and ownership — states cleanly in a single paragraph.
